question_set.question: Use trace_node with node_name equal to Engineering and use color_flows with nodes equal to #e74c3c, color equal to #e74c3c and use calculate_conversion_rate with node_name equal to On-Demand in order to know Analyze the cloud cost allocation patterns and identify optimization opportunities for reducing AWS spending.

answer.value: The AWS cost allocation analysis reveals several optimization opportunities: (1) EC2 dominates costs at $275K/month (55% of total), with significant On-Demand usage ($82K) that could be converted to Reserved or Savings Plans. (2) On-Demand pricing accounts for $175K (35%), the second largest purchase model, indicating potential for commitment-based discounts. (3) us-east-1 region consumes $242K (48.4%), suggesting consolidation opportunities. (4) Engineering department bears the highest cost burden at $235K (47%), primarily from Proj Alpha ($95K). (5) Proj Alpha is the most expensive project at $145K/month. Recommendations: (a) Convert On-Demand EC2 instances to Reserved Instances for potential 30-60% savings, (b) Implement auto-scaling for us-east-1 workloads, (c) Review Proj Alpha architecture for cost optimization, (d) Consider Spot instances for non-critical workloads to leverage the $78K already spent on Spot, (e) Evaluate Shared Infra costs ($127K) for potential multi-tenant optimization.

key_insights: Proj Alpha is most expensive at $145K/month

Color flows for EC2 to visualize the largest service cost
Calculate conversion rate at On-Demand to understand commitment efficiency
